steps.name: Carriage 3 (Z-Back): place 4 LM8UU bearings
steps.instructionText: Place four LM8UU linear bearings into one Z-Back carriage half-piece. Flanges must face outward â€” away from each other â€” so they sit flush in the lip of each pocket.

steps.name: Carriage 3: close the second carriage half
steps.instructionText: Place the second Z-Back carriage half onto the first, trapping the 4 bearings in their pockets. The small ribbed belt hole should sit directly beside the large smooth belt hole.

guidance.instructionText: Hold both Z-Back carriage halves firmly together and shake the assembly.
guidance.whyItMattersText: Compress the two halves by hand until there is no gap. Shake side-to-side and up-down for 2â€“3 seconds. No tools needed â€” this is a hand-compression test only.

guidance.instructionText: Insert a smooth guide rod through the Z-Back carriage and hold it so the rod is vertical.
guidance.whyItMattersText: The rod should slide or drop through with slight resistance â€” if you have to shake the carriage for the rod to move through, that's correct. Motors pull 20 lbs of belt force; the carriage must not slip too freely.

steps.name: Carriage 3: place bolts and thread nuts
steps.instructionText: Insert 2Ã— M6x18 bolts into the two top holes and 2Ã— M6x30 bolts into the two bottom holes. Thread one M6 nut onto each bolt finger-tight.

steps.name: Carriage 3: hand-tighten â€” prep for drill
steps.instructionText: Thread and finger-tighten all 4 bolts on the Z-Back carriage. Seat each bolt snug by hand before moving to the power drill â€” this prevents cross-threading and lets the drill finish the final torque cleanly.
